title: Night Dragon: raiding the oil majors

scenes.narration: [serious] For over a year, hackers secretly raided big oil companies.
It started by November 2009. In 2011, the security company McAfee exposed it. They called it Night Dragon.
The targets were oil and gas companies in America, Taiwan, Greece and Kazakhstan.
Their method was simple. First, trick emails fooled workers. Then old Windows weak spots let them in.

items: Old weak spots let them in

scenes.narration: Inside, they took control of computers. They copied secret oil field bids and money plans.
One clue: they mostly worked normal office hours. A man in Shandong, China, ran their computers.
McAfee said the tools came mainly from China, but named no government. The victims were never named.

facts.claim: McAfee reported in February 2011 that the Night Dragon attacks began by November 2009 and targeted oil and gas companies in the U.S., Taiwan, Greece and Kazakhstan; victims were not named

Attackers took information on operations, oil field bids and financing; an individual in Heze, Shandong province, provided servers used to control victims' computers; activity during weekday business hours suggested company men
Five global energy firms were confirmed victims; methods included social engineering, spear-phishing, Windows exploits and Trojans
McAfee CTO George Kurtz said the tools, techniques and network activities originated primarily in China; the state was a suspect but not proven
